speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic arthritis of the left wrist secondary to *Neisseria gonorrhoeae* (Gonococcal arthritis).

The clinical presentation of migratory polyarthralgia (knee), a new monoarthritis (wrist), fever, chills, and a recent camping trip suggests disseminated gonococcal infection. I will request a Gram stain and culture of the wrist synovial fluid, as well as nucleic acid amplification testing for gonorrhea and chlamydia to confirm the etiology.
